diagnostic_evidence.quote: For differential equations with independent variables $\mbx=(x^1,x^2,\ldots,x^p)\in X\subset \mathbb{R}^p$ and dependent variables $\mbu=(u^1,u^2,\ldots, u^q)\in U\subset \mathbb{R}^q$, a natural geometric structure is the trivial fibred manifold

If one pulls back the complex to the submanifold of (infinitely prolonged) solutions of a given system of PDEs, the vertical cohomology groups remain trivial, but some horizontal cohomology groups may be nontrivial.

issues.failure_explanation: A trivial product bundle need not have contractible base or fibre. For example, the allowed choice U=R²\{0} has a closed angular vertical one-form with nonzero integral around a fibre circle, so it is not vertically exact. Restriction to an equation manifold can also introduce fibre topology: the equation (u¹)²+(u²)²=1 gives circle fibres even when the ambient dependent-variable space is R². Thus the asserted global acyclicity, including its preservation under restriction, does not follow from the stated setting.

failure_location.quote: The cohomology groups of the augmented  variational bicomplex are all trivial, reflecting the topological triviality of $J^\infty(X\times U)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State these claims locally on suitable contractible coordinate neighbourhoods, including regular local fibre charts on the equation manifold, or impose the requisite global topological hypotheses.
issues.overall_effect: The differential review overstates global exactness and exactness on arbitrary equation manifolds; its local uses need not fail.
issues.title: Global exactness is asserted without topological hypotheses
issues.why_classification: The paper already adopts a local viewpoint for the ensuing differential applications, so an explicit locality restriction preserves those substantive applications without a new proof architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: A system of PDEs is \textit{multisymplectic} if there exists a vertically closed $(p-1,2)$-form $\omega$ such that $\upd_{\uph}\!\omega$ is zero on the solution submanifold (but not identically zero).

issues.failure_explanation: The construction proves conservation but does not prove the required nontriviality. In particular, a null Lagrangian, including L=0, has the entire jet space as its Euler–Lagrange solution manifold. No form can then have its horizontal derivative vanish on that solution manifold without vanishing identically. More generally, the displayed universal current can have identically zero horizontal derivative.

failure_location.quote: So every system of Euler--Lagrange equations is multisymplectic.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State that every Lagrangian produces a possibly trivial vertically closed conserved current, and assert multisymplecticity only when the stated nontriviality condition is verified.
issues.overall_effect: The universal conserved-current construction remains valid, but the unconditional classification of every Euler–Lagrange system as multisymplectic does not.
issues.title: The universal current need not satisfy the definition's nontriviality requirement
issues.why_classification: The supported repair preserves the universal current construction but withdraws a mathematical guarantee for allowed degenerate Lagrangians; it is more than a typographical correction.

issues.failure_explanation: Forward differences do not obey the linear transformation law needed for the claimed invariance. Already for p=1, change coordinates by m=-n. Since the difference of m is -Δ, naturality would transform the new forward difference of m² into (2n-1)Δ, whereas the original operator applied to n² gives (2n+1)Δ. The stated pointwise exterior algebra therefore does not make this operator invariant under GL(1,Z), let alone arbitrary lattice shears.

failure_location.quote: Both $\dDh$ and $\dv$ are invariant under all  allowable changes of the coordinates used to describe their respective spaces, namely $GL(p,\mathbb{Z})$ transformations of the base space $\mathbb{Z}^p$ and diffeomorphisms of $\mathbb{R}^q$ (prolonged to $\mathbb{Z}^p\times P(\mathbb{R}^q)$).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Treat the oriented forward generators as part of the fixed structure and restrict the invariance claim to transformations preserving that structure. Full GL(p,Z) naturality would require a different transformation or cochain construction.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed coordinate independence under all lattice basis changes fails, although the bicomplex identities remain valid relative to the chosen forward lattice directions.
issues.title: Forward exterior differences are not invariant under arbitrary lattice basis changes
issues.why_classification: A fixed-lattice theory survives, but the advertised transformation scope must be materially narrowed or supported by an additional construction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: As the augmented difference  variational bicomplex is exact, there exists a Hamiltonian function $H$ on $\mathbb{Z}\times P(\mathbb{R}^2)$ that satisfies

q_1-q_0=\frac{\partial H(n,q_0,p_1)}{\partial p_1},\qquad
p_1-p_0=-\,\frac{\partial H(n,q_0,p_1)}{\partial q_0}.

q_1-q_0=\frac{\partial H(n,q_0,p_0)}{\partial p_0},\qquad
p_0-p_{-1}=-\,\frac{\partial H(n,q_0,p_0)}{\partial q_0}.

issues.failure_explanation: Closedness on a symplectic graph does not ensure that (q₀,p₁) are coordinates on that graph. The symplectic map q₁=p₀, p₁=-q₀ is a counterexample: fixing (q₀,p₁) leaves p₀ arbitrary, so H_{p₁}(q₀,p₁) cannot equal q₁-q₀. In the reverse direction, an arbitrary smooth H need not define a map either: H=-qp in the displayed staggered equations forces q₁=0 and p₋₁=0 while leaving p₀ undetermined. Both failures concern missing regularity of the relevant graph projections.

failure_location.quote: Consequently, $H$ is a function of $(n,q_0,p_1)$ only.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Work locally on an evolution graph where the mixed projection (q₀,p₁) is nonsingular. When starting from H, impose the corresponding implicit-function condition, such as 1+H_{qp}≠0, before calling the relation a map.
issues.overall_effect: The unrestricted equivalence between symplectic maps and the displayed Hamiltonian representations, including their interpretation as executable maps, is not established.
issues.title: The symplectic-map and Hamiltonian correspondence lacks transversality hypotheses
issues.why_classification: A comparable local generating-function result follows after standard but substantive transversality restrictions; the unrestricted correspondence must be narrowed.

issues.failure_explanation: Vertical closedness and conservation do not imply this stencil or coefficient dependence. For p=1 and q=2, the ordinary form du₀¹∧du₀² is conserved by the first-order identity evolution, but on the unrestricted prolongation space it cannot equal a sum of du₋₁^α∧du₀^β terms: these are different independent exterior-basis components. Moreover, the declared space Z^p×U does not contain the shifted coordinates used on the right-hand side.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Make the standard nearest-neighbour form an explicit additional assumption and place it on the appropriate prolongation space, rather than deriving it from conservation of an arbitrary current.
issues.overall_effect: The purported converse and standard-form representation cover less than the arbitrary conserved currents introduced in their hypotheses.
issues.title: A general conserved current is incorrectly assigned the standard nearest-neighbour form
issues.why_classification: The subsequent standard-form theory remains usable, but the claimed normal-form generality must be withdrawn.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: (However, these equations may be weaker than the given system and so admit other solutions.)

issues.failure_explanation: Even granting a valid construction of an ambient Lagrangian, the displayed conclusion gives only inclusion of the original solutions among the Euler–Lagrange solutions, not the reverse inclusion. This distinction persists for linear systems and standard currents. For example, du₋₁∧du₀ is conserved by u₁=u₀ and also by u₁+u₋₁-2u₀=0. The latter is generated by L=u₀(u₁-u₀) and additionally admits nonconstant affine sequences. The current therefore does not determine the original solution set.

Now we are going to propose a systematic method, with which one can

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Withdraw equivalence and state only a compatible Euler–Lagrange system that may admit additional solutions. A genuine equivalence theorem requires further hypotheses and a converse argument not supplied here.
issues.overall_effect: The promised equivalent variational formulation, including the later unrestricted linear converse, is not supported. This defect remains even if the separate lifting step is repaired.
issues.title: Conservation of a current does not establish an equivalent Euler–Lagrange system
issues.why_classification: The supported weakening changes the central guarantee from equality of solution sets to one-way inclusion.

issues.failure_explanation: The interior Euler operator uses contractions with ambient coordinate vector fields, which need not be tangent to the equation manifold. It therefore cannot be applied to an equality known only after restriction. Explicitly, take u₁=u₀, η=u₋₁ du₀, and ℒ=n(u₁-u₀)Δ. On the constant-sequence solution manifold, both d_hη and d_vℒ vanish, so the required restricted equality holds. Nevertheless, the stated Euler formula gives E(ℒ)=(-n+(n-1))du₀∧Δ=-du₀∧Δ, which does not vanish there.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must construct an ambient extension of the restricted primitive and prove that its Euler–Lagrange form vanishes on the original equation manifold, rather than applying the Euler operator to a pulled-back equality.
issues.overall_effect: The proposed inverse procedure does not even establish that the constructed Euler–Lagrange equations are satisfied by the given solutions.
issues.title: The inverse construction applies the Euler operator to an on-solution identity
issues.why_classification: A nontrivial extension theorem or replacement inverse-variational argument is required; the source's exactness calculation does not supply one.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
This is exactly the same as the exterior difference
$\upd_{\uph}^{\vartriangle}$ we introduced
for the uniform lattice $\mathbb{Z}^p$.

issues.failure_explanation: For a general mesh, dividing an edge difference by its length approximates differentiation along that edge, not differentiation with respect to the corresponding physical coordinate. For example, take x_n=(hn¹,h(n¹+n²)). The first edge has length √2h, and its normalized difference tends to (∂_{x¹}+∂_{x²})/√2, not D₁. Edge lengths also omit the directional information needed to identify the rescaled symbols with dx^i. Cancellation of the scale factors proves an abstract lattice identity, not these componentwise geometric limits.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the asserted limits to suitable coordinate-aligned meshes with nonzero monotone steps, or introduce and justify a mesh Jacobian and appropriate geometric coframe for general meshes.
issues.overall_effect: The physical-coordinate interpretation on arbitrary metric or non-coordinate-aligned meshes is unsupported; the abstract bicomplex indexed by Z^p is not invalidated.
issues.title: Mesh distances alone do not give the claimed physical-coordinate differential limit
issues.why_classification: A comparable non-uniform coordinate-mesh theory survives, but the general geometric limit requires a substantive scope restriction or an additional construction.

issues.failure_explanation: The prolongation coordinates have arbitrary integer indices, whereas the displayed factorial definition is undefined for negative entries; negative powers of S-id in the subsequent homotopy are also not supplied. Merely interpreting all homotopy summation indices as nonnegative does not fix the stated identity. For p=1, l=1 and σ=d_vu₋₁, one has d_hσ=Δ∧(d_vu₀-d_vu₋₁), but every F^{I+1} with I≥0 vanishes, so the claimed left-hand side is zero rather than σ.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Specify the nonnegative-index range of the displayed formula and, in the exactness argument, first translate each finite-support form so that its vertical-form indices are nonnegative, apply the homotopy there, and translate the resulting primitive back.
issues.overall_effect: The supplied horizontal homotopy does not prove exactness for forms involving backward shifts, which are explicitly part of the paper's complex.
issues.title: The horizontal homotopy is not defined for the allowed negative shift indices
issues.why_classification: Finite support and commutation of shifts with the horizontal differential provide a short local bypass that retains the full exactness statement.
